summary: A search for one kind of file goes by a single list of extensions. In crates/fffinder-core/src/kind.rs, `KindFilter::accepts(&Path)` (the lower-cased extension is in `extensions()`; Any Kind takes every file, Folder none) replaces `KindFilter::matches(FileKind)`, which is gone. The lists are completed from `classify`'s arms: Code +22 (cjs, mm, pl, r, exs, erl, clj, htm, sass, less, bat, cmd, vim, el, nim, wgsl, glsl, metal, proto, graphql, cmake, mk), Archive +crate, Document +log, adoc, jsonl, nuon, ini, ods, plist, ron, env, conf, cfg, odp. Document keeps ppt, pptx and key and leaves out sqlite, sqlite3, db, parquet and lock, with a comment. `classify` is untouched. In crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, `search_root` checks each hit with `req.kind.accepts(&path)` and takes the kind's part of the query from a new private helper, `kind_tokens(kind, user)`. With no extension typed it is the kind's extensions, as before. With one typed (read with fff-search's own parser: a positive `*.ext` token) it is none of them, plus an exclusion `!*.ext` for each typed extension the kind doesn't have, so a typed extension narrows the kind inside fff-search instead of being ORed with it. docs/manual.md's Kind menu row says that a kind goes by the extension (so `README` and `Makefile` are found only with Any Kind), what Document covers, and that a typed extension narrows the kind.
changelog: The **Kind** menu missed files. **Document** never found a presentation (`.pptx`, `.ppt`, `.key`), and **Code**, **Archive** and **Document** left out extensions that fffinder shows with their icons, such as `.htm`, `.bat`, `.proto`, `.crate`, `.log` and `.jsonl`. Each kind now goes by one list of extensions. An extension typed in the search was ignored once a kind was chosen: with **Image**, `logo *.svg` listed every image named logo. It now narrows the kind, so that search lists only the SVG images, and `logo *.txt` lists nothing, in a Smart Folder saved that way too. `fff find --kind` and `fff open` follow the same rules. A name with no extension, such as `README`, is still found only with **Any Kind**.
behaviour_changes: All of these are for searches with a file kind chosen (Document, Image, Movie, Audio, Code, Archive): the Kind menu, Smart Folders, `GET /v1/find?kind=`, `fff find --kind` and `fff open`. Searches with Any Kind (with or without `type=file`) and Folder build the same query as before: 7,500 generated searches gave the same items and scores on the trunk and on this commit.

Document finds presentations: `.ppt`, `.pptx` and `.key` were listed but always dropped; `.odp` is new. In the demo folder with two decks added (162 files indexed), `deck` with Document listed 21 unrelated near misses and now lists `Kickoff deck.key` and `Launch deck.pptx`.

Document also finds `.log`, `.adoc`, `.jsonl`, `.nuon`, `.ini`, `.ods`, `.plist`, `.ron`, `.env`, `.conf`, `.cfg`. Still not found under Document: `.sqlite`, `.sqlite3`, `.db`, `.parquet`, `.lock`, and names with no extension.
Code also finds `.cjs .mm .pl .r .exs .erl .clj .htm .sass .less .bat .cmd .vim .el .nim .wgsl .glsl .metal .proto .graphql .cmake .mk`. Archive also finds `.crate`.
Where the wanted file is one of those, the typo-only near misses that were listed in its place are gone, because an exact match now exists.

A typed `*.ext` narrows the kind instead of being ignored. Image + `logo *.svg` lists only the SVG files named logo (before: every image named logo). Image + `*.svg` lists only SVG files (before: every image), also inside one searched folder and in a folder outside the search locations. Image + `logo *.txt` shows No Results (before: the images named logo). Image + `logo *.svg *.txt` lists the SVG files. Archive + `*.gz` no longer lists backup.zip. Code + `/notes/ *.md` lists nothing (before: notes/todo.rs). Document + `*.md *.rs` lists only the .md files.

What is no typed extension, so that the kind's whole list still applies beside it: an exclusion (`logo !*.png`), an escaped token (`\*.svg`), and globs (`*.{svg,txt}`, `*.s?g`, `art/**/*.svg`, `*.test.*`). With Letter case set to Smart or Ignore a two-part extension such as `*.tar.gz` is a glob as well; the results are the same as under case-sensitive, where it is an extension.

A Smart Folder, `fff find --kind X` or `fff open` whose words include an extension of another kind returned the whole kind and now returns nothing. `fff open budget *.csv` opens a CSV instead of the best document of any type.

While an extension is typed under a kind (`logo *.s`, `logo *.sv`) the window shows No Results until the extension is one of the kind's. Before, the kind's files stayed listed. Any Kind already behaves this way. `logo *` and `logo *.` still list the kind. A second extension being typed leaves the first one's files listed (`budget *.csv *.js` lists budget.csv).

Search memory: a kind search with a typed extension of that kind, and no folder searched, gets the opened-before boost under the typed text, as Any Kind searches do, because fff-search is given exactly what was typed (seen: score 1187 against 190 once the file had been opened from `logo *.svg`; the trunk gave no boost). A kind search with no extension typed still gets none, and neither does one in a searched folder or one with a typed extension the kind doesn't have.

Document results are noisier where there are `.log`, `.conf`, `.cfg`, `.env`, `.ini` and `.plist` files: source trees, and on macOS `~/Library` when the home folder is a search location. A private key such as `server.key` is found with Keynote files. `fff open` takes the top Document hit, so it can pick one of these; among equally good names fff-search puts the newer file first.
`total_matched` for a kind search is the number of matching files of the kind. A typed extension the kind doesn't have no longer counts toward it. Nothing shows this number.

Speed, on /usr with 78,804 indexed files (debug build, best of 15, run twice while the other lanes loaded the machine): Code + `main` 18 and 19 ms on the trunk, 28 and 21 ms on this commit, with 40,376 files matched against 36,378. Code + `main *.py` 19 and 18 ms against 15 and 15 ms. Code + `main *.txt` 21 and 18 ms against 1 ms. Document + `readme` 19 and 15 ms against 15 and 15 ms.
Not changed: icons, the Kind column's text, Group By Kind, previews (`classify` and `kind_label` are untouched), and contents searches, which have no kind.
Engine API (workspace-internal crate): `KindFilter::matches(FileKind)` is removed and `KindFilter::accepts(&Path)` added.
left_out: Names with no extension (`README`, `LICENSE`, `Makefile`) are still not found under a file kind. The manual says so; there is no second pass, as the plan says.
No test in tests/server.rs and no UI test, as the plan says. tests/server.rs's `kind=document` request and tests/basics.rs's click on Document pass unchanged.

The guard against `classify` learning an extension that a kind's list lacks is by samples (htm, proto, bat, crate, jsonl, nuon). A test can't walk `classify`'s match arms and the plan forbids restructuring it, so such an extension would get the kind's icon and not be found under the kind. The other direction is exhaustive: every listed extension is held to `classify`'s kind for it.
CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.
nu/fff.nu, docs/protocol.md, README.md and the Search Syntax dialog are unchanged. None states anything this makes wrong.
`kind_label` has no name for `.key` or `.odp` (the Kind column shows KEY File and ODP File), and a presentation keeps the plain file icon, because `classify` has no kind for one.
`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: nothing under src/term, src/macos.rs, src/win.rs or examples uses `KindFilter`, `matches`, `accepts` or `extensions` (grep is empty).
Only Linux was compiled. The change is plain Rust with no cfg.

notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit: 538 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. The trunk moved twice during the review. 9cf7635 (escape-ends-search) came before the first check, and 69b956f (history-menus) while it ran, which refused the first push; both rebases were clean, neither commit touches the engine or kind.rs, and the check was run again on the final commit. Pushed to origin (69b956f..65da066). No fix was folded in: I found nothing in the implementer's commit to change, so it is on the trunk as written, rebased.

How it was checked. (1) Tests without the change: the trunk's engine.rs and kind.rs above `mod tests`, under this commit's test modules, with two shims so that they compile (`accepts` as the trunk's two checks taken together, `kind_tokens` as the trunk's loop). 5 of the 6 new or rewritten tests fail, each at the assertion that names the problem; the sixth is a guard. (2) Seven mutations of the final code, one at a time; `tests` says what each test caught. One survives: with the per-hit `accepts` check taken out of search_root no test fails, because fff-search is only asked for files that `accepts` takes, so the check rejects nothing. It stays, as the plan says, as the one line that holds a search to what a kind is. (3) A model, written apart from the engine: 2,500 generated kind searches (words, capitals, typos, single letters, up to three typed extensions with two in three from the kind's own list, two-part and cut-off ones, negated extensions, globs, folder filters, quoted words, six scopes) on a tree of 2,543 files. With typos off, under Smart, case-sensitive and Ignore: each result is the files-only Any Kind search of the same text, kept to the files `accepts` takes; no difference in 7,500 comparisons, where the trunk's code differs 2,687 times in 2,500. With typos on (5,000 searches): every hit is of the kind and has a typed extension when one was typed. (4) Trunk and commit side by side through a probe (an example built in the lane and removed again): about 190 searches by hand on an 82-file fixture, each difference read; 480 odd ones under two case settings (other alphabets, a 2,000-letter word, sixty extensions, stray quotes, backslashes and slashes) with no panic; five searches typed letter by letter; folders outside the search locations; the opened-before boost with a database. (5) The lists against `classify`'s arms by script, both ways: the five single-kind lists equal their arms; Document differs by ppt, pptx, odp, key (list only) and sqlite, sqlite3, db, parquet, lock (left out on purpose). (6) Six screenshots of my own, light and dark: Document + `deck`, Image + `logo *.svg`, Image + `logo *.txt` (No Results, whose hint names the kind), Image + `logo *.s` while typing, Code + `beacon`, Document + `b`.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code says. (1) A kind search that lists less than expected with nothing to say why. A typed extension and a kind are now both required, which is the point; what counts as a typed extension is what fff-search's own parser reads as one, so an exclusion, an escaped token and a glob leave the kind's list in place, and the model found no kind search missing a file that the files-only search has and the kind takes. What a user will meet: No Results for two or three keystrokes while an extension is typed, and an old Smart Folder with a kind and another kind's extension, which now shows nothing. (2) Other files using up the hits fff-search is asked for, so that the kind's files are missing and nothing says so. The trunk had this (2,100 text files beside one image: an empty list), and the plan's variant would have kept it for two typed extensions. The exclusions keep those files out inside fff-search, and an exclusion can't take a file of the kind with it: it is only made for an extension whose last part the kind doesn't have, and every file it matches ends in that part. (3) Document filling up with files nobody calls documents, and `fff open` opening one. This is the brief's choice and I left it; see the doubts.

Doubts that remain. (a) What Document takes is a judgement the plan made: `.log`, `.conf`, `.cfg`, `.env`, `.ini`, `.plist`, `.ron`, and `.key`, which is also a private key. On a Mac whose home folder is a search location, `~/Library` holds thousands of `.plist` and `.log` files, and a Document search now matches them (a name that fits the words better still ranks first). Taking one out is an edit of one list. (b) `fff open` takes the top Document hit, which can now be a presentation, a log or a key; it could already be a PDF or a Markdown file. (c) An extension added to `classify` and not to a kind's list goes unnoticed by the tests, as said under left_out. (d) macOS and Windows were not compiled here.

For briefs still to come.
- query-history-boost: the text search_root gives fff-search for a file kind is the typed text, then `kind_tokens(req.kind, user)`, then the searched folder's glob. `kind_tokens` is empty when every typed extension is one of the kind's, so such a search with no folder searched is already looked up under the typed text and gets the boost; your case (b), Document with a plain word, still fails today. It adds ` !*.ext` for a typed extension the kind doesn't have. If you key by the typed text on both sides, nothing here is in the way.
- scoped-search-special-folder-names: `kind_tokens` is appended before the glob. If the glob stops being text, a file-kind search can be one token only when that token is a typed extension (`*.svg` with Image); a lone folder token always has the kind's extensions beside it, so it stays a filter there.
- result-tie-break, sorted-search-results: Image + `*.svg` has no word, so every hit has the same score. A kind search asks fff-search only for files of the kind, typed extensions of other kinds excluded, so `total_matched` is the number of matching files of the kind and the per-hit check drops nothing. See the first item under Found, not fixed.
- empty-state-messages: a kind with an extension of another kind (Image + `logo *.txt`) is a new way to reach No Results, also while an extension is being typed. Your Any Kind button fits it: with Any Kind that search lists the text files.
- smart-folder-save-and-leaks: a saved search with a kind and an extension of another kind showed the whole kind and now shows nothing. A leaked kind is easier to notice for the same reason: with Document left on, `*.png` finds nothing.
- typo-fallback-near-miss: the kinds find more exact matches, so fewer searches fall back to typo matches. `words` and the strict check are untouched. With a kind chosen the fallback is still what a user sees when no file of the kind has the words: `store` with Document lists server.key and sheet.ods where store.sqlite is the only real match.
- search-syntax-click-example: the example `*.pdf *.md` clicked with a kind chosen now lists only that kind's PDF and Markdown files, which is nothing unless the kind is Document. Assert on the search field's text, or leave the kind at Any Kind.
- live-search-results, multi-word-highlights, recents-walk-index, adhoc-index-feedback, search-settings-without-effect, regex-content-search (all in engine.rs): new in the file are `kind_tokens`, between `WithFolders`'s `impl ParserConfig` and `split_quoted`, and three tests after searches_a_folder. In search_root the kind's part of the query is one line, and the per-hit check is `req.kind.accepts(&path)`. `KindFilter::matches` is gone.
- image-preview-details: line numbers in kind.rs moved (the lists grew); `classify` is untouched.
- adhoc-index-feedback: see the last item under Found, not fixed, for the socket's side of what your brief says of the window. A kind search of a folder outside the search locations is the typed text and the kind's tokens with no glob, and a typed extension narrows the kind there too.

Found, not fixed (all on the trunk before this change).
- Results with the same score come in a different order from one run to the next when their files were last modified in the same second: fff-search breaks a tie by the modification time and then by what its threads returned first. Comparing the trunk with itself, 123 of 7,500 searches listed the same items in another order, and where the limit cuts through such a group, other members of it. This is result-tie-break's subject.
- A token that starts with `*.` and has a slash in it, such as `*.svg/`, is read by fff-search as an extension that no file has, so it finds nothing, with any kind.
- `GET /v1/find` with a `scope` outside the search locations (`fff find --here` or `--scope` there) searches the folder's temporary index without waiting for its scan: the server calls `Engine::search` once and returns the hits, and `Engine::prepare` has no caller. The first call can return nothing or a part of what is there; the window asks again, the socket doesn't. My probe fell into it until it called `prepare`. adhoc-index-feedback knows this for the window.
